Grief is emotional, but it is also a whole-body stress response, and her symptoms should not be dismissed as “just grief.”

The immediate priority is her chest tightness: chest discomfort, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, light-headedness, faintness, or pain spreading to the arm, back, jaw, shoulder, or upper abdomen should be assessed urgently by emergency services, even if anxiety or grief seems a plausible explanation. [shard_04785_27239] [shard_01997_39276]

This is particularly important because intense bereavement can trigger takotsubo, or “broken-heart,” cardiomyopathy, which commonly affects older women, can resemble a heart attack, and requires hospital assessment to distinguish it from one. [shard_01997_39276]

Grief activates the fight-or-flight system, increasing adrenaline, heart rate, breathing, blood pressure, and the work required of the heart. [shard_04122_13052] [shard_01169_7873]

The risk of a heart attack is highest in the first hours and days after a major loss, remains particularly relevant through the first weeks, and observational evidence suggests cardiovascular risk is still elevated during roughly the first three months. [shard_04122_13052] [shard_03619_28624]

At six weeks she is still within that higher-risk period, and missed blood-pressure tablets, poor sleep, reduced food intake, and disrupted medical routines can add avoidable strain. [shard_00754_37779] [shard_01169_7873]

Stress also activates the hypothalamus–pituitary–adrenal axis, releasing cortisol and other stress hormones that can alter sleep, appetite, blood-pressure regulation, metabolism, memory, and immune activity. [shard_03431_63689] [shard_03619_28624]

Cortisol may remain abnormal for months after bereavement, but this does not mean that every grieving person has chronically harmful hormone levels or that cortisol should be “treated” simply because grief is present. [shard_01169_7873] [shard_03761_73428]

In older bereaved adults, studies suggest changes in cortisol-related immune regulation, T-cells, natural-killer cells, and responses to vaccination, but the findings describe altered vulnerability at a population level rather than proof that grief has caused an infection or immune disease in one individual. [shard_03761_73428]

Inflammation is similarly complicated: short-term stress can temporarily suppress some immune functions, whereas prolonged or poorly regulated stress may make inflammatory control less effective and may aggravate existing conditions. [shard_03431_63689]

Sleep loss, inadequate nutrition, dehydration, alcohol, smoking, and missed medicines may therefore be as medically important as the emotional distress itself, without implying that her mourning is abnormal. [shard_05152_49859] [shard_01169_7873]

If the chest tightness is present now, recurrent, worsening, or accompanied by breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, sweating, nausea, or unusual weakness, the family should seek urgent assessment rather than arranging a routine appointment. [shard_04785_27239] [shard_01997_39276]

Even without emergency symptoms, she should have a prompt general-practitioner review for blood pressure, medication adherence and side effects, hydration and nutrition, sleep, mood, physical examination, and any heart symptoms, with an ECG or blood tests if the clinician considers them appropriate. [shard_03211_38194] [shard_01997_39276]

She should not restart, stop, double, or alter her blood-pressure medicine without advice, but a family member can help organise a medication list, pill box, reminders, pharmacy support, and transport to the appointment.

A doctor can also offer grief counselling, individual therapy, or a bereavement support group, and asking for this help does not medicalize ordinary mourning; it adds support while preserving her own way of grieving. [shard_03211_38194] [shard_02841_26140]

Practical support is usually more helpful than pressure to “move on”: regular small meals and fluids, gentle activity if medically safe, company, a simple sleep routine, help with appointments and household tasks, and avoiding alcohol or drugs are reasonable measures. [shard_04785_27239] [shard_05152_49859]

Sadness, low energy, appetite change, concentration problems, and disrupted sleep can occur in normal bereavement and may persist for many months, so their presence alone does not establish depression or a disorder. [shard_02610_47867]

Take additional mental-health warning signs seriously at any time, particularly hopelessness, wishing she had died, suicidal thoughts, inability to manage basic daily activities, severe isolation, confusion, or escalating alcohol or drug use. [shard_02610_47867] [shard_06347_54133]

If intense yearning, preoccupation with the deceased, hopelessness, disconnection, or inability to function remains disabling at six months or later, professional assessment for prolonged grief or depression is reasonable, while recognising that the purpose of treatment is to restore functioning rather than erase love or remembrance. [shard_02841_26140] [shard_06347_54133]
